title: High Cycle Fatigue Testing in Advanced Nanocrystalline Alloys
content: In situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM) experiments of high-cycle, load-controlled fatigue testing enable new insights into the origins of fatigue at the nanoscale. Initially, experiments with nanocrystalline Cu films established a foundational experimental approach for these nanoscale fatigue experiments [1]. Shortly after this development, investigations into Cu-Zr alloy films demonstrated the influence of grain boundary character on material fatigue behavior [2]. Most recently, nanoscale fatigue experiments on Pt films (and later confirmed with Cu films) revealed the phenomenon of crack healing, demonstrating the possibility of crack advancing, arresting, healing, and redirecting all while cyclic loading is applied [3]. These initial fatigue experiments have led to two primary types of results: the observation of anomalous nanoscale fatigue behavior, such as crack healing, or qualitative comparisons of materials with significantly different fatigue responses. Building on these prior investigations, there exists a need to further develop these nanoscale experiments to access further insights of nanoscale mechanisms of fatigue. The present work refines the process of in situ TEM fatigue by further developing the sample preparation and execution of fatigue experiments with the goal of being able to meaningfully compare the fatigue response of materials at the nanoscale.
